title: conducts and manages scientific studies
meaning_vi: tiến hành và quản lý các nghiên cứu khoa học

examples.en: A dedicated national body now conducts and manages scientific studies on public health threats.

title: pioneers in artificial intelligence
meaning_vi: những người tiên phong trong trí tuệ nhân tạo

examples.en: Countries that become pioneers in artificial intelligence often attract the largest share of global research funding.
Tackling antibiotic resistance is now regarded as one of the most urgent global challenges facing humanity.
International cooperation can accelerate progress towards solving humanity's most urgent scientific challenges.
Developing advanced technology for space travel requires decades of sustained investment.
Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to speed up drug discovery and diagnosis.
Open data sharing among researchers fosters innovation across multiple scientific disciplines.

title: invent the most advanced automobiles
meaning_vi: phát minh ra những chiếc ô tô tiên tiến nhất

examples.en: Engineers who invent the most advanced automobiles often rely on technology first developed for aerospace research.
Sustained investment in laboratories has led to a series of scientific breakthroughs in vaccine development.

title: solving pressing problems
meaning_vi: giải quyết những vấn đề cấp bách

examples.en: Scientific research plays an indispensable role in solving pressing problems that threaten public welfare.

title: renewable technologies
meaning_vi: công nghệ năng lượng tái tạo

examples.en: Governments are pouring billions into renewable technologies in a bid to cut carbon emissions.
Non-governmental companies now lead much of the world's research into renewable battery storage.
A serious dearth of accessible fossil fuel reserves has pushed many nations toward alternative energy sources.
Large-scale capital investment in offshore drilling has created thousands of jobs in coastal communities.
Itinerant workers often travel to remote drilling sites in search of higher wages in the energy industry.

title: remote region
meaning_vi: khu vực xa xôi hẻo lánh

examples.en: Drilling in remote regions has become increasingly common as easily accessible oil reserves dwindle.
Climate change is often described as an existential threat that scientific research must help address.
Communities have protested pipeline construction that cuts through their ancestral land.
Oil extraction frequently threatens fragile habitats that countless species depend on for survival.
Large-scale drilling projects can erode indigenous culture by disrupting traditional ways of life.
Supporters of fossil fuel expansion point to job creation as one of its most immediate benefits.
A single oil spill can devastate marine ecosystems for decades after the initial disaster.
Resource depletion has forced many countries to reconsider their long-term reliance on fossil fuels.

title: stimulate economic growth
meaning_vi: kích thích tăng trưởng kinh tế

examples.en: Investment in the energy sector can stimulate economic growth in otherwise underdeveloped regions.
A disruption to the supply pipeline can cause fuel prices to spike within days.

title: a deteriorating environment
meaning_vi: một môi trường đang xuống cấp

examples.en: A deteriorating environment poses an existential threat that scientific research alone cannot solve.

title: be pushed to the verge of destruction
term: be pushed to the verge of destruction
pronunciation: /biː pʊʃt tuː ðə vɜːdʒ ɒv dɪˈstrʌkʃn/
meaning_vi: bị đẩy đến bờ vực hủy diệt

examples.en: Without decisive action, fragile ecosystems could be pushed to the verge of destruction within a generation.

title: countless detrimental impacts of climate change
term: countless detrimental impacts of climate change
meaning_vi: vô số tác động tiêu cực của biến đổi khí hậu

examples.en: Researchers continue to document the countless detrimental impacts of climate change on global food security.
Coastal cities have suffered from widespread damage caused by increasingly severe storms.
New offshore drilling projects were launched to bolster supply amid rising global demand for oil.

title: enhance energy security
meaning_vi: tăng cường an ninh năng lượng

examples.en: Diversifying fuel sources can enhance energy security and reduce a nation's dependence on imports.

title: tackle the exhaustion of fossil fuel
term: tackle the exhaustion of fossil fuel
meaning_vi: giải quyết tình trạng cạn kiệt nhiên liệu hóa thạch

examples.en: Investing in renewables is one practical way to tackle the exhaustion of fossil fuel reserves.
Stricter pollution control measures have significantly improved air quality in several major cities.

title: revitalizing life on Earth
meaning_vi: hồi sinh sự sống trên Trái Đất

examples.en: Reforestation projects aimed at revitalizing life on Earth have shown promising results in degraded regions.
Governments should adopt stricter conservation measures over further incursions into vulnerable landscapes.
The origins of the universe remain an enigma that astronomers are still striving to unravel.

title: habitable planets
meaning_vi: những hành tinh có thể sinh sống được

examples.en: The discovery of habitable planets has reignited public fascination with the possibility of life beyond Earth.

title: humanity's most basic drives
meaning_vi: những động lực cơ bản nhất của nhân loại

examples.en: Curiosity about distant galaxies reflects one of humanity's most basic drives: the urge to understand our origins.
Humans seem to have an innate desire to explore beyond the boundaries of their own planet.

title: planets that could harbour life
meaning_vi: những hành tinh có thể chứa sự sống

examples.en: Astronomers continue to search for planets that could harbour life within our galaxy.
Private companies have played an increasingly dominant role in the aerospace industry over the past decade.

title: provide intellectual satisfaction for individuals
meaning_vi: mang lại sự thỏa mãn trí tuệ cho mỗi cá nhân

examples.en: Studying the origins of the universe can provide intellectual satisfaction for individuals who value pure discovery.
Space research has quietly transformed everyday technologies such as smartphone cameras and GPS.

title: technological and existential gain
meaning_vi: lợi ích công nghệ và sự tồn vong

examples.en: Proponents insist that the technological and existential gains of space travel far outweigh the price tag.
Satellite technology has found wide-ranging applications, from weather forecasting to disaster relief.
Many scientists regard the search for exoplanets as a worthwhile endeavour despite its enormous cost.
The scientific benefits of exploring distant planets often outweigh the initial financial outlay.
Space agencies view Mars settlement as a contingency plan should Earth ever become uninhabitable.

title: creating a more favorable living environment
term: creating a more favorable living environment
meaning_vi: tạo ra một môi trường sống thuận lợi hơn

examples.en: Some scientists dream of terraforming Mars, creating a more favorable living environment for future generations.
Real-time satellite imagery has become indispensable for disaster management during floods and wildfires.

title: explore new phenomena
meaning_vi: khám phá những hiện tượng mới

examples.en: Advanced telescopes allow astronomers to explore new phenomena at the edge of the observable universe.

title: interplanetary colonization
meaning_vi: công cuộc thực dân hóa liên hành tinh

examples.en: Proponents argue that interplanetary colonization could one day secure the survival of the human species.
Engineers are developing new propulsion systems that could make interplanetary travel far more efficient.
Some scientists argue that colonising other planets is essential for the long-term survival of our species.
Breakthroughs in materials science developed for spacecraft have since been applied to everyday consumer products.

title: NASA's recent ventures
meaning_vi: những dự án gần đây của NASA

examples.en: NASA's recent ventures into lunar exploration have reignited public interest in space travel.
Modern ships rely on satellite signals to navigate safely across the open ocean.
The invention of reusable rockets has dramatically lowered the cost of launching satellites into orbit.
Recent space missions have delivered valuable data on the composition of distant planets.
Asteroid mining is often cited as a potential avenue for funding future space missions.
Early-warning satellite systems have proven to be a genuine life-saving tool during hurricanes.
Some biotech firms look for profits above all else, which raises concerns about ethical oversight.

title: the invention of lab-grown meat
meaning_vi: phát minh thịt nuôi cấy trong phòng thí nghiệm

examples.en: The invention of lab-grown meat could drastically cut the environmental footprint of the food industry.

title: transformative technologies
meaning_vi: công nghệ mang tính đột phá

examples.en: Investment in transformative technologies such as gene editing could reshape medicine within a generation.
Billions of dollars are spent every year designing and launching satellites and rockets into orbit.

title: has many aspects to take care of
term: has many aspects to take care of
pronunciation: /hæz ˈmeni ˈæspekts tə teɪk keər əv/
meaning_vi: có nhiều khía cạnh phải quan tâm, xử lý

examples.en: Running a national laboratory has many aspects to take care of, from safety to long-term funding.

title: obscure theoretical field
meaning_vi: lĩnh vực lý thuyết khó hiểu, ít người biết đến

examples.en: Funding an obscure theoretical field may seem wasteful today, yet it can yield transformative discoveries decades later.

title: preferred to work individually
meaning_vi: thích làm việc độc lập hơn

examples.en: Some laboratories have preferred to work individually rather than risk losing credit for their discoveries.
Some argue that private institutions are far more efficient at directing important scientific research.
Critics who claim that scientific research wastes public funds often overlook its long-term societal value.
Critics question the practicality of crewed missions to Mars given the current budget constraints.

title: sustaining life on Earth
meaning_vi: duy trì sự sống trên Trái Đất

examples.en: Governments should not overlook the challenge of sustaining life on Earth while chasing ambitious space programmes.

title: terrestrial priorities
meaning_vi: những ưu tiên trên mặt đất (trần thế)

examples.en: Critics insist that terrestrial priorities such as poverty and healthcare should come before costly space missions.

title: at the expense of
meaning_vi: với cái giá phải trả là, đánh đổi bằng

examples.en: Funding ambitious space missions at the expense of basic public services is a controversial policy choice.

title: attract more talented and skillful scientists
term: attract more talented and skillful scientists
meaning_vi: thu hút thêm nhiều nhà khoa học tài năng và lành nghề

examples.en: Higher salaries in the private sector help attract more talented and skillful scientists away from universities.
Charities argue that meeting people's basic needs should take priority over ambitious scientific ventures.
Poor career prospects in academic research push many young scientists toward industry jobs instead.

title: competent technology experts
meaning_vi: chuyên gia công nghệ có năng lực

examples.en: Without more competent technology experts, industries will struggle to keep pace with global innovation.

title: compounded
meaning_vi: (verb (past participle)). trở nên trầm trọng hơn

examples.en: The teacher shortage is compounded by low salaries that fail to attract new graduates into science.
Diverting funds to planetary research inevitably starves critical public services such as education and healthcare.
Many students find the maths required for physics courses simply too daunting to attempt.
Extreme destitution in some regions makes lavish space budgets seem almost indefensible.
High tuition fees can deter talented students from enrolling in demanding science degrees.
Building a new particle accelerator involves an enormous cost that few nations can bear alone.
Scientists and engineers are widely regarded as essential drivers of a country's economic growth.

title: exorbitant costs
meaning_vi: chi phí cắt cổ, quá đắt đỏ

examples.en: Critics argue that the exorbitant costs of certain research programmes are difficult to justify to taxpayers.

title: government-run operations
meaning_vi: các hoạt động do chính phủ điều hành

examples.en: Critics claim that government-run operations are often slower to innovate than their private-sector counterparts.
Governmental companies are often criticised for being slower to innovate than private rivals.
Bureaucratic red tape continues to hamper the approval of promising new treatments.
A shortage of skilled researchers will inevitably hinder progress in fighting emerging diseases.
The immediacy of a famine leaves little room for governments to justify long-term research spending.

title: immediate issues
meaning_vi: vấn đề cấp bách trước mắt

examples.en: Local governments are often forced to prioritise immediate issues such as housing over long-term research.
A shortage of qualified scientists carries serious implications for a nation's long-term competitiveness.
Engineering and physics are often seen as intimidating majors that only the most confident students choose.

title: journal paywall
meaning_vi: tường phí truy cập tạp chí khoa học

examples.en: A journal paywall often prevents researchers in developing countries from accessing the latest findings.
A lack of transparency in how research grants are awarded has fuelled public distrust of scientific institutions.

title: limited or uncertain benefit
meaning_vi: lợi ích hạn chế hoặc không chắc chắn

examples.en: Opponents claim that deep-sea exploration offers only a limited or uncertain benefit compared with its cost.

title: misallocation of resources
meaning_vi: sự phân bổ sai nguồn lực

examples.en: A misallocation of resources occurs whenever large budgets are devoted to projects with little practical relevance.

title: misunderstandings and confusion among scientists
meaning_vi: sự hiểu lầm và bối rối giữa các nhà khoa học

examples.en: Language barriers frequently cause misunderstandings and confusion among scientists working on shared projects.
The opportunity cost of funding space exploration is a reduction in spending on domestic infrastructure.
The perception that science is only for gifted students discourages many capable learners from pursuing it.
Many taxpayers feel that pressing issues at home deserve funding before ambitious missions to Mars.

title: pressing social problem
meaning_vi: vấn đề xã hội cấp bách

examples.en: Homelessness remains a pressing social problem that many governments have failed to resolve.

title: public dissatisfaction
meaning_vi: sự bất mãn của công chúng

examples.en: Public dissatisfaction with research spending tends to grow whenever projects fail to deliver visible outcomes.

title: refused to share their research
meaning_vi: từ chối chia sẻ nghiên cứu của họ

examples.en: Certain corporations have refused to share their research for fear of losing a competitive edge.

title: render the process costly and ineffective
term: render the process costly and ineffective
meaning_vi: khiến quá trình tốn kém và kém hiệu quả

examples.en: Bureaucratic red tape can render the process costly and ineffective for scientists seeking cross-border funding.

title: roadblocks to international scientific collaborations
meaning_vi: rào cản đối với hợp tác khoa học quốc tế

examples.en: Conflicting regulations remain among the biggest roadblocks to international scientific collaborations.

title: scientific collaborative activities
meaning_vi: hoạt động hợp tác khoa học

examples.en: Opponents of scientific collaborative activities claim that differing national interests often derail joint projects.
The stereotype that science is only for exceptionally gifted people puts off many capable students.
Critics argue that taxpayer money should not be spent on projects that yield no visible public return.

title: underfunded education system
meaning_vi: hệ thống giáo dục thiếu kinh phí

examples.en: An underfunded education system struggles to produce the scientists a country needs for future innovation.

title: unjustified
meaning_vi: không chính đáng, không có cơ sở

examples.en: Many taxpayers feel that lavish spending on space tourism is largely unjustified.

title: urgent human need
meaning_vi: nhu cầu cấp thiết của con người

examples.en: Some argue that scarce funds should first address urgent human needs like clean water and nutrition.

title: wider societal benefit
meaning_vi: lợi ích rộng lớn hơn cho xã hội

examples.en: Funding basic science can deliver a wider societal benefit that is not immediately obvious to policymakers.

title: a more structured learning environment
meaning_vi: môi trường học tập có cấu trúc hơn

examples.en: Some pupils thrive in science only when given a more structured learning environment with clear guidance.

title: abandon global efforts
meaning_vi: từ bỏ những nỗ lực toàn cầu

examples.en: It would be short-sighted to abandon global efforts to combat climate change simply because progress is slow.

title: acquire unique resources and scientific expertise
term: acquire unique resources and scientific expertise
meaning_vi: thu được nguồn lực độc đáo và chuyên môn khoa học

examples.en: By partnering with foreign universities, a country can acquire unique resources and scientific expertise it lacks domestically.

title: agree on the terms of collaboration
term: agree on the terms of collaboration
meaning_vi: thống nhất về các điều khoản hợp tác

examples.en: Research teams from different nations must agree on the terms of collaboration before sharing sensitive data.

title: benefit the population
meaning_vi: mang lại lợi ích cho dân chúng

examples.en: Research grants should be directed towards projects that genuinely benefit the population, such as affordable healthcare.

title: dedicate time and financial resources to tackling issues
term: dedicate time and financial resources to tackling issues
pronunciation: /ˈdedɪkeɪt taɪm ənd faɪˈnænʃl rɪˈsɔːsɪz tuː ˈtæklɪŋ ˈɪʃuːz/
meaning_vi: dành thời gian và nguồn lực tài chính để giải quyết vấn đề

examples.en: Nations must dedicate time and financial resources to tackling issues such as rising sea levels.
Some governments prefer to delegate large-scale research projects to private firms with specialised expertise.

title: poverty alleviation programs
meaning_vi: chương trình xóa đói giảm nghèo

examples.en: Redirecting research budgets into poverty alleviation programs could lift millions out of hardship.
Many universities now partner with businesses to bring scientific products to market more quickly.

title: underserved region
meaning_vi: khu vực chưa được phục vụ đầy đủ

examples.en: Mobile health clinics have brought basic medical care to many underserved regions.

title: without worrying about the depletion of resources
term: without worrying about the depletion of resources
pronunciation: /wɪˈðaʊt ˈwʌriɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə dɪˈpliːʃn əv rɪˈsɔːsɪz/
meaning_vi: mà không phải lo lắng về sự cạn kiệt tài nguyên

examples.en: State-funded labs can pursue long-term research without worrying about the depletion of resources.
Many economists view spending on vaccine research as a thoroughly worthwhile investment.

title: prevent wasteful expenses
meaning_vi: ngăn ngừa chi tiêu lãng phí

examples.en: Stricter budget oversight was introduced to prevent wasteful expenses in publicly funded research programmes.
